newsitem.title: USA: Southern Calif. utilities encourage electric cars.
newsitem.headline: Southern Calif. utilities encourage electric cars.

text.p: Southern California's electric utilities hailed the start Thursday of retail marketing of electric-powered vehicles.

"We have put in place rate options to provide EV (electric vehicle) owners an incentive to charge EVs during the night," said Howard Levin, energy products manager for Enova Corp's San Diego Gas and Electric Co.

General Motors on Thursday became the first major auto manufacuturer to begin retail marketing of an electric car, the EV1, which is being offered for lease through Saturn dealerships in San Diego, Los Angeles and Phoenix, Ariz.
Despite continued reservations about their limited mileage range and high production costs, other major automakers plan to begin selling the no-emission cars next year and in 1998.
Enova announced Thursday plans to begin developing a network of public charging stations for electric vehicles in SDG&E's service territory, albeit with a fairly modest $50,000 initial investment.
California utilities sought, but were largely denied, approval to raise customer rates by millions of dollars in order to fund infrastructure investment for natural gas- and electric-fueled vehicles.

The California Public Utilities Commission agreed with consumer advocates and others who argued that shareholders should bear the risk of promoting and developing a new market for electricity and slashed the funding requests.
But some still argue that tax incentives and other subsidies to the industry are inherently unfair.

Californians Against Hidden Taxes, a coalition including the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association and the California Manufacturers Association, said the GM model is aimed at an elite few in the six-figure income bracket.
The coalition estimates rebates and tax incentives for the EV1 - which has a sticker price near $34,000 - of $7,500.

But Southern California Edison Co, the electric utility subsidiary of Edison International welcomed the GM move as the an example of innovative technology that is driving the evolution of the industry.
Edison is also working to support and develop installation of electrical systems needed for widespread EV use.
